info.name: SuperCalPlan
info.summary: Plans your Nextcloud tasks into free calendar time (a fork of CalPlan)
info.description:
SuperCalPlan is a fork of [CalPlan](https://github.com/corbin-auriti/calplan) by Corbin Auriti, with fixes and more features: a Duration field and daily limits in Tasks, working hours in the settings, task trees planned in order, tasks split into parts when they do not fit whole, re-planning as soon as a calendar event changes, and planned times shown in Tasks. It uses the same task tags and calendar blocks as CalPlan, so switching keeps your plan: disable CalPlan before enabling SuperCalPlan (your CalPlan settings are copied on install).
SuperCalPlan finds time for your Nextcloud tasks. Turn on **Auto-schedule** for a task and SuperCalPlan adds a `🔒 Task title` time block to the first free place in your working hours. When you edit or finish the task, SuperCalPlan updates or removes the block.
**Important setup:** put scheduled tasks in a calendar/list that supports **both tasks and events** (`VTODO` + `VEVENT`). No calendar shows an event stored in a Tasks-only list, so SuperCalPlan gives such tasks no block and flags them as not scheduled. In Nextcloud Tasks, choose a normal calendar that supports tasks—not a Tasks-only list. SuperCalPlan plans and writes only in your own calendars; calendars shared with you, subscriptions and federated calendars count as busy time.
**How it works** 1. Open a task in Nextcloud Tasks and turn on **Auto-schedule** (or add the standard `calplan` tag from another CalDAV client). 2. SuperCalPlan checks your calendars for busy time and finds a free block. Personal exclusions can completely remove selected calendars from SuperCalPlan or make ordinary events with selected titles stop counting as busy. 3. It writes one derived event for that task. The task remains the source of truth: edit the task, not the calendar block. 4. Completing, cancelling, or untagging the task removes its block on the next reconcile.
Task start and due dates are respected. The default block is 30 minutes; set the Duration field SuperCalPlan adds to the Tasks sidebar (saved as `ESTIMATED-DURATION`), a standard iCalendar `DURATION`, or a notes line such as `Duration: 15min` or `Duration: 1hr`. Tasks can be split into parts, limited per day, and planned as trees whose subtasks follow each other. A `First step:` notes line is shown as `👣 First step:` in the slot; legacy `Next:` lines remain supported. Help buttons beside Reconcile and Auto-schedule explain these helpers.
After a task block ends, SuperCalPlan can add a filterable `calplan-review` (“Is complete?”) task tag and either try another time or pause Auto-schedule, according to your personal setting. Personal limits can cap both task minutes and task-block count per day. Ignored calendars are completely outside SuperCalPlan: their tasks, events, tags, and existing blocks are not read or changed. Ignored event-title rules are case-insensitive and can use exact or contains matching; they affect ordinary busy events only, never tasks or SuperCalPlan blocks. The Reconcile help shows the latest run, while Personal settings keeps privacy-safe diagnostics for the latest ten runs. SuperCalPlan is self-contained, uses standard iCalendar properties, and does not patch the Tasks or Calendar apps. Task and calendar-event edits reconcile immediately. Other calendar clients refresh on their own sync interval, so you may need to press refresh there to see a new or removed block right away.
